Title: A finite averaging bound.
Discipline/article type: elementary mathematical exposition, theoretical note.

## Objective and contribution
This pedagogical note illustrates a standard finite-average argument. No claim of original discovery or application to infinite sequences is made.

## Proposition
Let n be a positive integer and x_1, ..., x_n be real numbers. At least one index j in {1, ..., n} satisfies x_j >= (x_1 + ... + x_n)/n.

## Proof
Write m = (x_1 + ... + x_n)/n. If no such index existed, x_i < m for every i in {1, ..., n}. Summing these finitely many strict inequalities gives x_1 + ... + x_n < n*m. By definition of m the two sides are equal. This is a contradiction, so such an index exists.

## Boundary and scope
For n=1 equality holds. All x_i may coincide, also giving equality. The proof uses only finite sums of real numbers and n>0; it asserts neither uniqueness of j nor any result about infinite sums.

## Conclusion
At least one member of a nonempty finite real list is at least its average. This simple argument can help introduce contradiction proofs.
